trap-nonspeakable.notes: TWO NUMERICAL ERRORS IN THE FINAL SENTENCE, both verified independently at 40 dps by building the Gram matrix from prop:frobenius-gram-matrix and applying the star (which swaps L+ and L-). The block says: 'At q_0 under convention D the star-form spectrum is 0, 0.752702^{x3}, 4.230339: exactly one null direction, and it is the braid-symmetric one.' (1) MULTIPLICITY: the star form's spectrum is 0, 0.75270211 with multiplicity FOUR, 4.2303392 — six eigenvalues for a six-dimensional form, signature (5,0,1), which is what prop:frobenius-gram-matrix reports. The quoted x3 lists only five eigenvalues, and x3 is the multiplicity of +0.75270211 in the BILINEAR spectrum (-0.75270211, 0, +0.75270211 x3, +4.23033920). So the bilinear multiplicity has been carried into a star-form sentence — precisely the confusion prop:frobenius-gram-matrix warns about when it says any statement about the signature must name its pairing. (2) THE NULL DIRECTION IS ANTI-SYMMETRIC, NOT SYMMETRIC. The kernel vector, computed and then normalised, is (1, -0.900918284, -0.900918284, 0.8116537544, 0.8116537544, -0.7312337075) on the NF basis (gamma, sigma_0, sigma_1, L+, L-, e-). Those are exactly (-1/q)^length: -1/q = -0.900918284, 1/q^2 = 0.8116537544, -1/q^3 = -0.7312337075, matching to ten digits. That is the q-ANTIsymmetriser, i.e. the (1^3) alternating block — which is what rem:frobenius-gram-matrix-context and prop:frobenius-gram-matrix both identify as the radical (y_{(1^3)} = 0 under convention D). The braid-symmetric direction would have coefficients q^length = 1.110, 1.232, 1.368, all positive, and is not in the kernel. Fix: 'exactly one null direction, and it is the braid-antisymmetric one — the (1^3) block'.
